note: golden_hash filled by golden-parity.test.mjs --update. Worked examples (hand-verified arithmetic): subject premium (caller-supplied total manual premium plus premium items subject to experience rating) times the experience modification, rounded to whole dollars per the pinned Whole Dollars - Premiums rule. Vector 4 is the mod-0 case from the experience-modification node's undetermined-rating output (EXPMOD_ZERO_DENOMINATOR): it must flag and never yield a premium. Vector 5 is the non-finite gate. Vector 6 is the negative-subject-premium gate. No NCCI or state rate table value appears here -- every licensed value is an input.

vectors.name: credit_mod_credit_risk
vectors.description: Subject premium $10,000, mod 0.90 -> modified premium $9,000 (exact whole dollars).

output_payload.regulatory_basis: NCCI Basic Manual premium algorithm as published by the Indiana Compensation Rating Bureau (Premium Algorithms): add to manual premium all premium items subject to experience rating to get total subject premium, then apply the experience modification to arrive at the modified premium; premiums shown to the nearest dollar, a remainder of $0.50 or more rounded to the next higher dollar (WCRB Wisconsin Workers Compensation and Employers Liability Basic Manual, Whole Dollars - Premiums).
output_payload.note: Subject premium composition is the caller's responsibility -- this kernel does not compute manual premium from payrolls and rates, and never vendors or reproduces NCCI or state rate tables. Out of scope: premium discount, expense constant, terrorism/catastrophe surcharges, state taxes, schedule rating and assigned-risk surcharge. The NCCI algorithm does not apply in the monopolistic state funds (Ohio, North Dakota, Washington, Wyoming) or the Puerto Rico and USVI funds.
